value.rationale: An irreducible central isotypic projection has a canonical, sharply attained nonabelian Fourier endpoint amplification invariant. Unlike a neighboring two-row block, the hook character has a genuinely two-variable negative region with unbounded transposition count; the exact all-rank norm and supergeometric convergence to an explicit Poisson-tail constant quantify Fourier stability beyond the classical character table.
